limitations: The Human Protein Atlas records relative normalized RNA expression levels (nTPM), relative mass-spectrometry peptide/protein intensities, and relative tumour vs normal differential abundance (CPTAC log2FC). It does not measure absolute copy numbers, molecular masses, cell volumes, or absolute protein molecules per cell. Absolute molecule counts per cell and absolute molecule ratios cannot be mathematically derived from relative MS intensities and nTPM values without external absolute calibration…

A missing record in HPA (e.g., CPTAC rows for MT-ND1, HBA2, CD52 or MS intensity for CD52, EPAS1) represents an unmeasured/unreported assay in that dataset rather than zero abundance or biological absence.

limitations: The Human Protein Atlas provides relative measurements: normalized transcript abundance (nTPM in rna_tissue_consensus.tsv), relative mass-spectrometry signal intensity (Intensity in ms_tissue.tsv), and relative differential protein abundance (log2 fold change in cancer_cptac.tsv). Absolute copy numbers (molecules per cell) and absolute protein-to-RNA molecule counts cannot be calculated from these relative levels without external spike-in standards, cell volume metrics, or absolute calibration c…

MS intensity and RNA nTPM reflect bulk lung tissue profiling, whereas CPTAC represents differential abundance between lung adenocarcinoma and paired normal tissue. Relative changes cannot be combined cross-assay into absolute molecular inventories per cell.
